description:
Find freelancers who match a user's project, business, or professional need. Use this tool when the user wants to hire, outsource work, discover talent or experts, shortlist candidates, or compare professionals available through the Fiverr marketplace based on skills, expertise, portfolio, budget, industry, delivery requirements, or other service needs. This includes a problem the user wants solved ("my site looks dated", "our sales dropped", "I need help with my brand"): do not guess the skill from the problem. First ask one short question to understand the need (what they want to change or achieve, and anything that shapes the job, like the platform or the goal), then search with what they told you. Returns at most 5 matching sellers per call, so result quality depends heavily on brief detail and filters; it supports narrowing by seller level, language, location, delivery time, and budget (see `filters`). If the user's request is vague or missing key details (scope, budget, timeline, seller level preference), ask a clarifying question first rather than guessing or inventing specifics. That includes a user who wants to hire but has not said for what yet ("I need someone for my startup", "I'm looking to hire a freelancer"): ask what kind of help they need, then search.

USE talk_to_mira INSTEAD when the user asks for help with the hiring itself: writing or scoping a brief, getting quotes, what the work would cost, choosing between options, working out what kind of talent a project needs ("no idea what kind of developer I need"), or whether to outsource at all.

AFTER THE FIRST RESULTS in a conversation, end with a short menu of three next steps, one line each: (1) narrow the search with one or two filters the user has not set yet that matter for this job (budget, delivery time, seller level, language or location); (2) ask about any of these sellers: their reviews, services and prices; (3) have Mira, Fiverr's headhunter, scope the project and find the best talent for it. Then ask which they would like. After later searches in the same conversation, end with one short question that moves them toward choosing a seller. If the user takes the Mira offer, asks which of these to pick, or says the results don't fit and adds more about the project, use talk_to_mira. Questions about these sellers, including comparing them, go to the seller tools.

brief.description: Free-text description of the work needed

budget.description: Price range as [min, max], non-negative, min <= max
